name: Telemark Windblock Anorak
description:
A pullover anorak in a wind-resistant bonded softshell, cut long through the body with a half-zip neck, a large kangaroo pocket across the front, and a drop hem in the back. The colorway is a faded slate blue that reads almost grey in low light. Telemark is a Scandinavian-heritage outdoor label with a GLMZ distribution office — their pieces are designed for people who spend time outside in actual weather, not people who want to look like they do.

The anorak construction eliminates the front zipper and most hardware, making it warmer and simpler to care for. It's a Tier 2 to Tier 3 crossover piece — cheap enough that a working-class outer-district resident buys it for commuting through the lakefront wind corridors, cool enough that a Tier 3 urbanist wears it on a weekend without irony. It layers over a hoodie, under a heavier shell, or alone in shoulder season.
what_it_says: You prioritize function and you've thought about what you actually need rather than what looks impressive. Quietly competent.
story_hooks: The Telemark distribution warehouse in the port district has been receiving shipments with extra units that don't appear on any manifest — someone is using the supply chain to move something.

A character realizes that everyone at a particular the Gray Zone-district mutual aid meeting is wearing the same Telemark anorak — it's become an unintentional uniform, and a corponation security team has noticed.

A Telemark rep approaches a character who's been wearing their jacket in a high-visibility situation, offering an unusual amount of money for the specific jacket off their back — just the one they're wearing.

physical_description.visual_profile: A relaxed, slightly oversized pullover jacket with a distinctly minimalist Scandinavian silhouette. The long body and dropped back hem create an elongated line that reads casual but intentional. The half-zip collar and absence of front closure hardware give it an understated, utilitarian appearance—contemporary outdoor wear rather than fashion statement.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the shoulders and chest, with enough room for layering. Long in the body with a noticeable drop hem at the back, creating a slight A-line. Not baggy, but definitely not fitted—designed for movement and weatherproofing rather than body definition.
physical_description.primary_material: Bonded softshell synthetic composite—technically engineered polymer laminate with a brushed micro-fleece backing. Wind-resistant but breathable, lacking the stiffness of hardshell jackets.
physical_description.texture: Smooth face with a subtle directional nap; the interior has a soft, slightly fuzzy brushed finish. Seams are visible but cleanly finished. No quilting or padding—the warmth comes from the material itself and trapping air layers.
physical_description.color_scheme: Faded slate blue with cool undertones, desaturated enough to read as grey-blue in dim urban lighting or overcast lakeside conditions. Uniform color with no visible pattern or contrast panels.
physical_description.closures: Half-zip neck closure (likely plastic or anodized metal slider, minimal branding). No front zipper or buttons—the design relies on pullover entry. Likely internal friction-fit or elastic at cuffs and hem.
distinctive_features: Large kangaroo pocket spanning most of the front—deep, practical, not decorative
Half-zip neck allowing quick ventilation without full front exposure
Dropped hem in back, extending 2-3 inches below front hem
Minimal hardware and branding—Telemark label visible only as a small woven tag inside or embroidered subtly at shoulder
Visible stitching that signals durability rather than luxury
Thumb loops or cuff cinches (implied by utility-first design)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 crossover. Affordable enough for working-class commuters (Tier 3), but premium enough in construction and heritage that Tier 2 corpo-adjacent urbanists wear it unironically.
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals practical outdoor engagement, stability, and a rejection of purely aesthetic fashion. Worn by lakefront commuters, mid-level warehouse workers, ecological researchers, and young professionals who value function over logo. Marked Scandinavian heritage appeals to GLMZ residents with Northern European ancestry or those seeking non-corpo authenticity.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in after a few months of regular wear. Slight fading in high-friction areas (collar, cuffs), maybe small snags or pilling on the brushed interior. No major damage—these jackets are built to last years of commute abuse. Smells faintly of lake wind and urban precipitation.
